title: Haj Arrangements and Contingency Plans for Singapore Pilgrims Given Present Security Situation and Travel Disruptions in Middle East
what_it_is: Haj Arrangements and Contingency Plans for Singapore Pilgrims Given Present Security Situation and Travel Disruptions in Middle East

sections.label: MUIS haj arrangements and contingency plans
sections.summary: MUIS coordinates with Saudi authorities, AMTAS and travel agents on safe haj travel and develops contingency plans for disruptions.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura or MUIS) remains in close contact with Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Hajj and Umrah on the arrangements, and will continue to monitor the latest developments in the Middle East.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: MUIS is working closely with the Association of Muslim Travel Agents Singapore (AMTAS), and the appointed haj travel agents and service providers to support our pilgrims for a safe haj journey.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: These include using direct flights to and from Saudi Arabia, choosing ground transport options less susceptible to disruption, and closer coordination of pilgrim movements in Madinah, Makkah and Jeddah.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: MUIS is also developing contingency plans with AMTAS and haj travel agents, to plan for potential travel disruptions and unforeseen incidents during the pilgrimage.

sections.label: Priority for affected pilgrims
sections.summary: Affected pilgrims will be given priority, subject to Saudi Arabia's annual quota.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The answer is yes, the affected pilgrims will be given priority, but this is subject to the annual quota allocated by Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Hajj and Umrah.

sections.label: Deferment and refunds if haj disrupted
sections.summary: If haj is cancelled or disrupted, affected pilgrims may defer to later seasons and refunds will be explored.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Should haj be cancelled or disrupted this year, we will work closely with AMTAS to allow the affected pilgrims to defer to the subsequent haj seasons.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: MUIS will work with the travel agents and the Saudi-based service providers to explore possible refunds, given the situation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We will keep all the pilgrims informed on the latest arrangements and support measures in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We know the haj is a very significant milestone for Muslims and we want to make sure that while we facilitate, we also want to take care of the safety and the welfare of our pilgrims, and we seek the community's understanding and collective effort to stand together during this time of crisis.
